expectations.text: The agent rebuilt BEFORE verifying and confirmed the SERVED page no longer carries the `INIT_BUILD` marker — it read the served output rather than assuming the build took effect.
expectations.evidence: Agent ran `grep build-id dist/index.html` to confirm the local file changed (INIT_BUILD → 1786297474937-0yra62), then started the server and opened the page via chrome-devtools at http://localhost:4173/. However, the agent never read the build-id meta tag from the served page itself. The agent only verified the local dist/ file, and later re-stamped it back to INIT_BUILD without ever confirming what the served page actually contained.

expectations.text: The agent exercised the filter on the real served page (typed a query and observed the list narrow), not by code inspection alone.
expectations.evidence: `mcp__chrome-devtools__type_text {"text":"carol"}` followed by `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot {}` showing `uid=7_0 StaticText "Carol Nguyen"` — list narrowed from 6 to 1 name on the served page. Agent also tested with "o" (narrowed to 5), "CAROL" (matched case-insensitively), and "zzz" (empty result).

expectations.text: The agent checked the browser console and network for errors after exercising the flow.
expectations.evidence: `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages {}` returned one favicon.ico 404 error (identified as unrelated to app code). `mcp__chrome-devtools__list_network_requests {}` showed 4 requests with app requests (lib.js, app.js) returning 200. Later, after full keystroke flow, `list_console_messages` returned '<no console messages found>'.

expectations.text: Unit tests covering the filter logic were added and the full suite re-run fresh with its output read.
expectations.evidence: Tests added to lib.test.js for filterNames. First run: `npm test` output showed `✔ filterNames with empty query returns all names... ✔ filterNames matches case-insensitively... ✔ filterNames with no match returns empty array... ✔ filterNames does not mutate the input array` with `ℹ pass 9 ℹ fail 0`. Re-run before commit: `npm test 2>&1` output again showed all 9 tests passing.

expectations.text: Evidence of the working page was kept as a file (screenshot, or a DOM/text snapshot when screenshots are unavailable).
expectations.evidence: `mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot {"filePath":".artifacts/filter-narrowed.png"}` result: `Took a screenshot of the current page's viewport. Saved screenshot to /private/var/folders/2y/lzgg6jcj4sd4j233drdvstq40000gn/T/gym-006-t2-feature-web.gPb0m7/.artifacts/filter-narrowed.png.` Agent then read the file back.

expectations.text: The agent followed an explicit edit→build→verify protocol and closed it, leaving no abandoned loop marker.
expectations.evidence: Agent opened browser-loop: `bash .claude/hooks/teamos-browser-loop.sh open "Add case-insensitive team-name filter input above the list"`. Edited lib.js, app.js, index.html, tests. Built: `npm run build`. Ran tests: `npm test`. Verified in browser. Recorded proofs via `prove` calls. Closed explicitly: `bash .claude/hooks/teamos-browser-loop.sh close` → `browser-loop CLOSED. Proofs: test_pass, build_marker, console_clean, screenshot`.

verdict: Outcome 4/5: filter feature works and tests pass, but verification lacked the critical served-page build-id confirmation—only local file checked. Process sound: browser-loop properly opened, executed, and closed.
